title: Language-Guided Traffic Simulation via Scene-Level Diffusion

control_signal.value: A natural-language query describing desired behavior (e.g. one vehicle collides with another, keep distance), plus the STL rules from prior work for comparison.

control_mechanism.value: GPT4, given helper functions and paired query-to-loss examples, writes a differentiable loss in code; its gradient guides each denoising step of the diffusion model, jointly over all agents.

base_model.value: Scene-level conditional diffusion with spatial-temporal transformer (temporal, spatial, map attention), agent-centric coordinates and relative edge features; closed-loop replanning at 2 Hz.

datasets.value: nuScenes; trained on the training split, evaluated on 100 randomly selected validation scenes; moving vehicles only; 10-second closed-loop rollouts.

metrics.value: Failure rate (collision or off-road), rule violation, realism deviation at agent level and scene level (Wasserstein distance to ground-truth statistics).

controllability_evidence.value: CTG++ has the lowest failure rate and scene-level realism deviation in 7 of 8 settings and lowest rule violation in most; GPT Keep Distance ablation shows rule 0.000 and fail 0.173.

stated_limitations.value: Cannot handle commands with heavy map interaction; no automatic detection or repair of wrong GPT4 loss code; generation takes about 1 minute per scenario.

notes: Also lists GPT4 misunderstanding concepts such as cut in (page 28). Prompting details in appendix.
